claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films or nanoribbons have significant residual interfacial strain.
As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films or nanoribbons have a high density of structural defects.
Residual interfacial strain impedes a reversible magneto-structural transition in these nanoscale alloys.
Defect-induced magnetic-domain pinning impedes a reversible magneto-structural transition.
Interfacial strain and defects create heterogeneous nucleation sites.
Strain, heterogeneous nucleation, and domain pinning broaden the magnetic or magneto-structural transition.
The as-deposited nanoscale state exhibits pronounced hysteresis.
The as-deposited nanoscale state has a muted magnetocaloric response compared with bulk forms.
Post-deposition thermal annealing will relieve residual interfacial strain.
Post-deposition thermal annealing will reduce structural-defect density.
Reducing strain and defect density will make the phase transition more spatially uniform and reversible.
Annealed samples will have a sharper magneto-structural transition than as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit less hysteresis, evidenced by a narrower hysteresis loop, than as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit a larger isothermal magnetic entropy change than as-deposited samples.
The proposed mechanism applies to films thinner than 100 nm or comparably sized nanoribbons under applied magnetic fields below 100 mT.
Magnetic-cooling cycle frequency must be limited by the system's heat-transfer rate.
The proposed relationship may not hold at elevated magnetic fields, during rapid cycling, or after extensive annealing-induced microstructural alteration.
